origin.description: Provides basic information on a given time zone identifier.

arguments.name: tz
arguments.text: NULL or "" for the default time zone, or one time zone identifier.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: NULL or "" for the default locale, or one locale identifier.

arguments.name: display_type
arguments.text: A unique prefix of short, long, generic_short, generic_long, gmt_short, gmt_long, common, or generic_location.

origin.details: The list has ID, Name, Name.Daylight, Name.Windows, RawOffset, and UsesDaylightTime. RawOffset is hours before daylight saving. Name.Daylight is missing when the zone does not use daylight time this year.
origin.example:
info <- stri_timezone_info("Europe/London", locale = "en_US")
cat(paste0("stri_timezone_info(\"Europe/London\", locale = \"en_US\")$Name is ", info$Name, ".\n"))

translation.description: Identifier, display name, Windows id, raw offset, and daylight use.

arguments.name: tz
arguments.text: None or "" for the default ICU zone, or one zone identifier.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: None or "" for the default locale, or one locale identifier.

arguments.name: display_type
arguments.text: A unique prefix of short, long, generic_short, generic_long, gmt_short, gmt_long, common, or generic_location.

translation.details: Name.Daylight is NA when the zone does not use daylight time. Name.Windows is NA when ICU has no Windows id. RawOffset is hours. UsesDaylightTime is a bool.
translation.value: A dict with ID, Name, Name.Daylight, Name.Windows, RawOffset, and UsesDaylightTime.
translation.example:
from stringi.datetime import stri_timezone_info
info = stri_timezone_info("Europe/London", locale="en_US")
print(f'stri_timezone_info("Europe/London", locale = "en_US")$Name is {info["Name"]}.')
